But just as the immortal work of John Bunyan had a very real support in truths and influences of the highest power and the deepest meaning, so the pages which record Mr.

arxiv-2107-14656.title: Fast Bayesian inference for large occupancy data sets, using the Pólya-Gamma scheme
arxiv-2107-14656.creator: Alex Diana 1,∗, Emily B. Dennis 2,1,∗∗, Eleni Matechou 1,∗∗∗ and Byron J.T. Morgan 1,∗∗∗∗ 1 School of Mathematics, Statistics and Actuarial Science, University of Kent, Canterbury, CT2 7FS, UK. 2 Butterfly Conservation, Manor Yard, East Lulworth, Wareham, Dorset, BH20 5QP, UK
arxiv-2107-14656.description: Abstract In recent years, the study of species’ occurrence has benefited from the increased availability of large-scale citizen-science data. Whilst abundance data from standardized monitoring schemes are biased towards well-studied taxa and locations, opportunistic data are available for many taxonomic groups, from a large number of locations and across long timescales.

arxiv-2203-02317.title: Adaptive Discounting of Implicit Language Models in RNN-Transducers
arxiv-2203-02317.creator: Vinit Unni, Shreya Khare, Ashish Mittal, Preethi Jyothi, Sunita Sarawagi, Samarth Bharadwaj
arxiv-2203-02317.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vinit Unni, Shreya Khare, Ashish Mittal, Preethi Jyothi, Sunita Sarawagi, Samarth Bharadwaj. RNN-Transducer (RNN-T) models have become synonymous with streaming end-to-end ASR systems. While they perform competitively on a number of evaluation categories, rare words pose a serious challenge to RNN-T models. One main reason for the degradation in performance on rare words is that the language model (LM) internal to RNN-Ts can become overconfident and lead to hallucinated predictions that are acoustically inconsistent with the underlying speech.

arxiv-2209-08102.title: Dark matter solution to the H 0 H_{0} and S 8 S_{8} tensions, and the integrated Sachs-Wolfe void anomaly
arxiv-2209-08102.creator: Krishna Naidoo, Mariana Jaber, Wojciech A. Hellwing, Maciej Bilicki
arxiv-2209-08102.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Krishna Naidoo, Mariana Jaber, Wojciech A. Hellwing, Maciej Bilicki. We consider a phenomenological model of dark matter with an equation-of-state w w that is negative and changing at late times. arxiv-2301-12485.title: Generating Novel, Designable, and Diverse Protein Structures by Equivariantly Diffusing Oriented Residue Clouds
arxiv-2301-12485.creator: Yeqing Lin, Mohammed AlQuraishi
arxiv-2301-12485.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yeqing Lin, Mohammed AlQuraishi. Proteins power a vast array of functional processes in living cells. The capability to create new proteins with designed structures and functions would thus enable the engineering of cellular behavior and development of protein-based therapeutics and materials. Structure-based protein design aims to find structures that are designable (can be realized by a protein sequence), novel (have dissimilar geometry from natural proteins), and diverse (span a wide range of geometries).

arxiv-2306-15999.title: On the energy density in quantum mechanics
arxiv-2306-15999.creator: Francisco Torres Arvizu, Adrian Ortega, Hernán Larralde
arxiv-2306-15999.description: Abstract There are several definitions of energy density in quantum mechanics. These yield expressions that differ locally, but all satisfy a continuity equation and integrate to the value of the expected energy of the system under consideration. Thus, the question of whether there are physical grounds to choose one definition over another arises naturally.

arxiv-2406-07555.title: Sequential Monte Carlo for Cut-Bayesian Posterior Computation
arxiv-2406-07555.creator: Joseph Mathews, Giri Gopalan, James Gattiker, Sean Smith, Devin Francom
arxiv-2406-07555.description: Abstract We propose a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) method to efficiently and accurately compute cut-Bayesian posterior quantities of interest, variations of standard Bayesian approaches constructed primarily to account for model misspecification. We prove finite sample concentration bounds for estimators derived from the proposed method and apply these results to a realistic setting where a computer model is misspecified.

arxiv-2411-07821.title: Population growth on a time varying network.
arxiv-2411-07821.creator: Michel Benaim, Claude Lobry, Tewfik Sari, Edouard Strickler
arxiv-2411-07821.description: Abstract We consider a population spreading across a finite number of sites. Individuals can move from one site to the other according to a network (oriented links between the sites) that vary periodically over time. On each site, the population experiences a growth rate which is also periodically time varying.

arxiv-2412-19146.title: AskChart: Universal Chart Understanding through Textual Enhancement
arxiv-2412-19146.creator: Xudong Yang, Yifan Wu, Yizhang Zhu, Nan Tang, Yuyu Luo
arxiv-2412-19146.description: Abstract Chart understanding tasks such as ChartQA and Chart-to-Text involve automatically extracting and interpreting key information from charts, enabling users to query or convert visual data into structured formats. State-of-the-art approaches primarily focus on visual cues from chart images, failing to explicitly incorporate rich textual information (e.g., data labels and axis labels) embedded within the charts.

arxiv-2503-07014.title: Vib2Mol: from vibrational spectra to molecular structures—a unified deep learning framework
arxiv-2503-07014.creator: Xinyu Lu, Hao Ma, Hui Li, Jia Li, Yi Rong, Yuqiang Li, Tong Zhu, Guokun Liu, Bin Ren
arxiv-2503-07014.description: Abstract There will be a paradigm shift in chemical and biological research, to be enabled by autonomous, closed-loop, real-time self-directed decision-making experimentation. Spectrum-to-structure correlation, which is to elucidate molecular structures with spectral information, is the core step in understanding the experimental results and to close the loop.

arxiv-2601-13238.title: A Semantic Decoupling–Based Two-Stage Rainy-Day Attack for Revealing Weather Robustness Deficiencies in Vision–Language Models
arxiv-2601-13238.creator: Chengyin Hu Xiang Chen Zhe Jia Weiwen Shi Fengyu Zhang Jiujiang Guo Yiwei Wei
arxiv-2601-13238.description: Abstract Vision–Language Models (VLMs) are trained on image–text pairs collected under canonical visual conditions and achieve strong performance on multimodal tasks. However, their robustness to real–world weather conditions, and the stability of cross–modal semantic alignment under such structured perturbations, remain insufficiently studied.

pmc-12566041.title: Blood Flow Restriction Training in Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review of Current Evidence on Postoperative Muscle Strength and Function
pmc-12566041.creator: Bassem Tiss, Saoussen Layouni, Hela Ghali, Halil İbrahim Ceylan, Iheb Nticha, Sonia Jemni, Raul Ioan Muntean, Nicola Luigi Bragazzi, Ismail Dergaa
pmc-12566041.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and Objectives: Knee arthroplasty often leads to marked postoperative muscle weakness, with strength losses of up to 62% in the first month, contributing to functional impairment and patient dissatisfaction. Blood flow restriction (BFR) training, which combines low-load exercise with partial vascular occlusion, has shown promise in enhancing muscle strength across musculoskeletal conditions and may represent a valuable rehabilitation strategy for this vulnerable population.

pmc-12588001.creator: Olivia Monton, Emmanuel F Drabo, Taleaa Masroor, Shannon Fuller, Alison P Woods, Amn Siddiqi, Tracy B Malone, Fabian M Johnston
pmc-12588001.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionDespite increasing palliative care capabilities in the USA, utilisation rates remain low for patients with advanced cancer, particularly among African American patients. To address this gap, a theory-driven, stakeholder-informed community health worker (CHW) palliative care intervention for African American patients with advanced cancer and their informal caregivers is currently being assessed through a hybrid type 1 effectiveness-implementation trial at four cancer centres across the USA.

pmc-13016912.description: BackgroundChildren and adolescents with HIV have lower treatment success than adults. Suboptimal adherence and resistance to antiretroviral therapy (ART) are known aetiological factors. This preplanned analysis in the GIVE MOVE trial (NCT04233242) describes drug resistance patterns in children and adolescents in Lesotho and Tanzania.

pmc-13048560.title: Drug–microbiome interactions: What we know and why predictive translation remains elusive
pmc-13048560.creator: Fatima C Pereira, Sahar El Aidy
pmc-13048560.description: Medication-induced alterations of the gut microbiome influence drug efficacy, toxicity, and long-term outcomes. Despite extensive evidence for drug-microbe interactions, predictive translation into clinical practice remains limited. Generalization from shifts in taxonomic profiles, mechanistic studies or isolated enzymatic assays is challenging because microbial activity is highly context-dependent.

uslaw-usc-t16-s2905.title: 16 U.S.C. § 2905 — Reimbursement of State costs for developing, revising, and implementing conservation plans and implementing certain nongame fish and wildlife conservation actions
uslaw-usc-t16-s2905.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s2905.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 49 (Fish And Wildlife Conservation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In general Any State may apply to the Secretary for reimbursement under this section for costs incurred by the State for the following: (1) The development of a conservation plan. (2) The revision of an approved conservation plan. (3) The implementation of nongame fish.
